subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What scope should OpenClaw accept for this native-Linux VPS reasoning-latency investigation before work proceeds?
rationale: The issue is valid and aligned with performance priorities, but the requested outcome spans docs, measurement environment, telemetry, agent prep, memory, compaction, Telegram, hooks, auth fallback, and OS tuning; automation cannot choose the acceptance bar safely.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a bounded docs/runbook path using existing diagnostics and identify measured gaps before opening optimization PRs.

options.title: Sponsor targeted instrumentation
options.body: Choose specific missing spans or metrics now, such as memory-search query timing or bundle-MCP subspans, and route each as a narrow implementation item.

options.title: Decline as support-specific
options.body: Close or redirect the request if maintainers do not want repository-owned analysis for one native VPS configuration.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded docs/runbook path using existing diagnostics and identify measured gaps before opening optimization PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad docs, diagnostics, queue, memory, and reliability history in this checkout routes most strongly through steipete for scope-setting.
